A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NearID research. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and corresponding equations, experiments, tables and figures can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original NearID, MTG and DreamBench++ evaluations, including trained-model results, loss and data ablations, and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds a controlled training-time foreground-masking ablation in Appendix E.6 and Table 7.

M1.justification: The proposed frozen SigLIP2 backbone, trainable MAP head, two-component contrastive objective and role-specific masking probabilities remain unchanged. v2 evaluates a masking-disabled control while retaining the original training recipe.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same SynCD-derived NearID data, MTG and DreamBench++, with the same generator coverage. Full-image and foreground-only evaluation already appear in v1; the new masking ablation uses this existing coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 7 adds NearID trained without foreground masking as a comparison control alongside default NearID and frozen SigLIP2. Comparator membership in the retained benchmark, loss-ablation and VLM-scaling experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: The new masking control sets all training masking probabilities to zero while keeping other hyperparameters identical. The KernelPCA visualization also changes its sample from seven identities in v1 Figure 5 to twelve in v2 Figure 6. Existing benchmark splits, metrics and training budgets are retained.

E4.justification: New Appendix E.6 and Table 7 test whether training-time foreground masking contributes to background-independent discrimination and part-level alignment. The embedding visualization is expanded to twelve identities; existing loss, data-source, masking-at-evaluation and hyperparameter analyses remain.

E5.justification: Fisher-z correlation aggregation, Table 2's plus/minus reporting and fixed-seed VLM evaluation are unchanged. The added masking ablation introduces no repeated-run information, uncertainty estimates or significance tests.

E6.justification: Retained numerical result tables are unchanged. New Table 7 reports foreground-only MTG oracle correlation of 0.391 without training masking versus 0.641 with it, and MTG SSR of 21% versus 32%, despite full-image NearID SSR of 99.8% versus 99.2%. The revised embedding plot also supplies a different twelve-identity visualization.

T1.justification: The loss definitions, discriminability margins, SSR/PA definitions, Fisher-z aggregation and positive-cohesion equations remain mathematically unchanged. No new theorem, proof or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction replace 'the first principled framework' with 'a principled framework for matched-context identity confusion,' narrowing the priority claim. The three principal contributions and headline performance claims are retained.

C2.justification: v2 explains lighter masking for positives and attributes masking's benefit specifically to foreground-only part-level transfer, while acknowledging that full-image NearID discrimination remains high without it. The conclusion adds explicit limitations concerning specialized domains, inpainting fidelity and style-conditioned identity; the earlier editing-scope discussion remains.

D1.justification: v2 documents the added control's reproducible configuration: retrain with masking probability zero and otherwise identical settings. Section 3.3 also explicitly clarifies that front and back views of the same instance are positives. Existing optimizer, synthesis, hardware, timing and project-access disclosures remain.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds CustomContrast and distinguishes its jointly trained generator encoder from NearID's standalone identity metric. RealCustom++ and Less-to-More Generalization are also newly cited. These are limited additions to the existing research positioning, accompanied by softened priority wording.

P1.justification: v2 makes targeted abstract, introduction and dataset-description edits, adds a source-datasets paragraph and masking subsection, and inserts conclusion limitations. The overall narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds masking-ablation Table 7 and redraws the KernelPCA plot with twelve identities and revised axes and legend. The contrastive-paradigm diagram moves from v1 Appendix A, Figure 6, to v2 main-text Figure 4 with a shorter caption. Other displays are retained with reflow and renumbering.

improvement.justification: The added masking ablation supplies controlled evidence missing in v1 for an existing training ingredient, distinguishing its foreground-transfer benefit from already saturated full-image discrimination. Clearer data explanations, closer prior-work positioning and specific limitations also improve assessability. These are limited gains: the main method and retained benchmark results are unchanged, and the new ablation provides no uncertainty estimates.
